task: Review CO forms for any express cost nondisclosure or overriding disclosure terms; not main agreement interpretation
finding: No express cost nondisclosure, audit prohibition, receipt waiver or override of main-agreement itemized/support-documentation language found in reviewed CO1–9 forms. Standard forms have a blank Backup Attached? field inside CCS Use Only. This field alone is not an owner audit or full-invoice-access right.
pricing: Standard forms show scope description and fixed total, not actual-cost reimbursement mechanism. Flooring CO shows quantity1 and fixed price $16,870 with express written authorization for additional flooring conditions. It does not waive expense-documentation requests or claim confidentiality.

CO10.scope: Bounded local search, not proof it does not exist
CO10.finding: PDF2 includes CO10 $3,356.40 within total final invoice $52,184.44; PDF3 aggregates $3,356.40 as this-month approved changes. Neither is CO10 executed scope form or supporting receipts.

troy_nov19.quote:
This project was contracted on a lump sum basis. The approved change orders and contract reconciliation establish the adjustments to the contract price.

Carney is not obligated under the agreement to disclose its internal subcontractor invoices, vendor pricing, or proprietary cost information.

The request for individual subcontractor quotations, detailed labor and material breakdowns, vendor contacts, and internal invoices is excessive and unnecessary to determine the cost of completing the remaining agreed punch list items.

We will provide the reasonable completion-cost estimate contemplated by Sections 9.1.7 and 9.1.12, but we will not produce internal subcontractor invoices or require our vendors to prepare additional quotations solely to support withholding payment.
troy_nov19.interpretation: This is Troy’s position in correspondence; it is not itself a cited nondisclosure clause or executed CO amendment.
